name: jwt
description: JSON Web Tokens and JWS: HS256, HS384, HS512 and EdDSA, strict parsing, claim validation with leeway, typed keys bound to one algorithm, and JWKS

api.name: JwtErr
api.sig: pub type JwtErr = Malformed{why: Str} | TooLarge{len: Int, max: Int} | UnsupportedAlg{alg: Str} | AlgNotAllowed{alg: Str} | UnknownCritical{name: Str} | NoKey{kid: Opt[Str]} | BadSignature | Expired{exp: Int, now: Int} | NotYetValid{nbf: Int, now: Int} | IssuedInFuture{iat: Int, now: Int} | IssuedTooLongAgo{iat: Int, max_age: Int} | WrongIssuer{iss: Opt[Str]} | WrongAudience{aud: List[Str]} | WrongSubject{sub: Opt[Str]} | WrongType{typ: Opt[Str]} | MissingClaim{name: Str} | BadClaim{name: Str, why: Str} | InvalidKey{why: Str} | BadJwks{why: Str} derive Eq, Show
api.doc: Why a token, a key or a key set was refused.

api.name: sha384
api.doc: The SHA-384 digest (48 bytes) of `data`, FIPS 180-4.

api.name: hmac_sha384
api.sig: fn hmac_sha384(key: Secret[Bytes], data: Bytes) -> Bytes
api.doc: HMAC-SHA-384 (RFC 2104, RFC 4231) of `data` under `key`: 48 bytes.

api.name: JsonValue
api.sig: pub type JsonValue = JNull | JBool{value: Bool} | JNum{text: Str} | JStr{value: Str} | JArr{items: List[JsonValue]} | JObj{fields: List[(Str, JsonValue)]} derive Eq, Show
api.doc:
A JSON value as parsed from a token, keeping the members of an object in their order and
numbers as their text (so nothing is lost or rounded).

api.name: parse_json
api.doc:
Parses JSON text (RFC 8259) strictly: one value, nested at most 32 deep, no duplicate member
names in an object, no lone surrogates, nothing after the value. `err` says what is wrong.

api.name: json_text
api.doc:
The compact JSON text of `v`: no spaces, members in order, strings escaped as RFC 8259
requires (quote, backslash and control characters), other characters as they are.

api.name: jint
api.doc: A JSON number for an integer.

api.name: jstr
api.doc: A JSON string.

api.name: member
api.sig: fn member(v: JsonValue, name: Str) -> Opt[JsonValue]
api.doc: The member `name` of an object, or none (also for values that are not objects).

api.name: json_int
api.doc:
The integer a JSON number denotes, rounded down when it has a fraction or an exponent
(NumericDate values may be fractional), or none when it doesn't fit in an Int.

api.name: b64url
api.doc: `b` as unpadded base64url, the encoding of every JWS segment.

api.name: from_b64url
api.doc:
The bytes of a canonical unpadded base64url segment: only `A-Z a-z 0-9 - _`, no padding, no
whitespace, and unused trailing bits zero. Anything else is none.

api.name: Alg
api.sig: pub type Alg = HS256 | HS384 | HS512 | EdDSA derive Eq, Show
api.doc:
A JWS algorithm this package implements: HMAC with SHA-256, SHA-384 or SHA-512, and EdDSA
with Ed25519.

api.name: alg_name
api.doc: The `alg` header value of `a`.

api.name: alg_of
api.doc:
The algorithm an `alg` header value names, matched exactly (names are case-sensitive), or none.
`none` and every algorithm this package doesn't implement are none.

api.name: all_algs
api.doc: Every algorithm, for a policy that accepts whatever the keys allow.

api.name: Key
api.sig: pub type Key = HmacKey{alg: Alg, kid: Opt[Str], mac_key: KeyBytes} | EdSigningKey{kid: Opt[Str], seed: KeyBytes, x: Bytes} | EdVerifyingKey{kid: Opt[Str], x: Bytes} derive Eq, Show
api.doc:
A key, bound to exactly one algorithm: an HMAC secret for `alg`, an Ed25519 signing key (its
32-byte secret seed and public key `x`), or an Ed25519 verifying key. `kid` is the key id that
tokens name in their header. Keys hold secrets, which can't be compared or printed, so `Key`
has hand-written `Eq` (secrets compared in constant time) and `Show` (secrets shown as
`<secret>`) instead of derived ones. Build keys with `hmac_key`, `ed25519_signing_key` and
`ed25519_verifying_key`, which check them.

api.name: KeyBytes
api.doc:
Secret key material, so keys can derive `Eq` and `Show`: it prints as `<secret>` (a `Key`
shows it as `KeyBytes(<secret>)`), and two `KeyBytes` compare in constant time. Unwrap with
`.raw`.

api.name: impl Eq for KeyBytes
api.doc: Equal when the bytes are, compared in constant time.

api.name: impl Show for KeyBytes
api.doc: Always `<secret>`.

api.name: hmac_key
api.sig: fn hmac_key(alg: Alg, k: Secret[Bytes]) -> Res[Key, JwtErr]
api.doc:
An HMAC key for `alg` (HS256, HS384 or HS512). RFC 7518 section 3.2 requires a key at least as
long as the hash: 32, 48 or 64 bytes.

api.name: ed25519_signing_key
api.doc: An Ed25519 signing key from its 32-byte secret seed (the JWK `d`).

api.name: ed25519_verifying_key
api.doc: An Ed25519 verifying key from its 32-byte public key (the JWK `x`).

api.name: generate_hmac_key
api.sig: fn generate_hmac_key(alg: Alg) -> Res[Key, JwtErr] ! rand
api.doc: A new random HMAC key of the minimum size for `alg`.

api.name: generate_ed25519_key
api.doc: A new random Ed25519 signing key.

api.name: with_kid
api.sig: fn with_kid(k: Key, kid: Str where _.len > 0) -> Key
api.doc: `k` with the key id `kid`.

api.name: key_alg
api.doc: The algorithm `k` is bound to.

api.name: key_id
api.doc: The key id of `k`, if it has one.

api.name: can_sign
api.doc: Whether `k` can sign: HMAC keys and Ed25519 signing keys can, verifying keys can't.

api.name: verifying_key
api.doc:
The key that verifies what `k` signs and may be given to others: the verifying key of an
Ed25519 signing key, `k` itself for a verifying key, and none for an HMAC key, whose verifier
is the secret itself.

api.name: public_bytes
api.doc: The public key bytes of an Ed25519 key, none for an HMAC key.

api.name: select_keys
api.sig: fn select_keys(keys: List[Key], kid: Opt[Str], alg: Alg) -> List[Key]
api.doc:
The keys of `keys` that may verify a token with algorithm `alg` and key id `kid`: bound to
`alg`, and when `kid` is given, carrying that id.

api.name: Policy
api.sig: pub type Policy = {algs: List[Alg], leeway: Int where _ >= 0, max_age: Opt[Int], issuers: List[Str], audiences: List[Str], subject: Opt[Str], typ: Opt[Str], required: List[Str], critical: List[Str], max_len: Int where _ > 0} derive Eq, Show
api.doc:
What verification accepts. `algs` is the allowlist (the header's `alg` must be in it and match
the key's); `leeway` is the clock skew allowed, in seconds, for `exp`, `nbf` and `iat`;
`max_age` limits how old `iat` may be; `issuers` and `audiences`, when not empty, are the
accepted `iss` values and the audiences of which `aud` must contain one; `subject` and `typ`
pin `sub` and the header's `typ`; `required` lists claims that must be present; `critical`
lists the `crit` header extensions the caller understands; `max_len` bounds the token length.

api.name: policy
api.doc:
A policy that accepts `algs` and checks only the time claims that are present, with no leeway
and tokens of at most 8192 characters. Add requirements with `with`.

api.name: Jws
api.sig: pub type Jws = {header: JsonValue, payload: Str, alg: Alg, kid: Opt[Str]} derive Eq, Show
api.doc:
A verified (or, from `decode_unverified`, merely decoded) JWS: its protected header, its
payload as text, and the algorithm and key id it named.

api.name: jws_verify
api.sig: fn jws_verify(token: Str, keys: List[Key], p: Policy) -> Res[Jws, JwtErr]
api.doc:
Verifies a compact JWS with `keys` under policy `p`'s `algs`, `critical` and `max_len`. The
header's `alg` must be in `p.algs`; then only keys bound to that algorithm, with the header's
`kid` when it has one, are tried. The payload can be any text; `verify` adds the JWT rules.

api.name: sign_compact
api.sig: fn sign_compact(k: Key, header: Str, payload: Str) -> Res[Str, JwtErr]
api.doc:
Signs `payload` with the exact header text `header`, which must be a JSON object whose `alg`
is `k`'s algorithm. For reproducing tokens byte for byte; `jws_sign` and `sign` build the
header themselves.

api.name: jws_sign
api.sig: fn jws_sign(k: Key, extra: List[(Str, JsonValue)], payload: Str) -> Res[Str, JwtErr]
api.doc:
Signs `payload` (any text) as a compact JWS: the header is `alg` from the key, `kid` when the
key has one, then `extra` (which may not set `alg`, `kid`, `crit` or `b64`).

api.name: decode_unverified
api.sig: fn decode_unverified(token: Str, max_len: Int where _ > 0) -> Res[Jws, JwtErr]
api.doc:
Decodes a token without checking its signature, for reading its header (`kid`, `alg`) before
choosing keys, or for debugging. Never trust what it returns. Parsing is as strict as
`jws_verify`'s, with no `crit` extension understood.

api.name: Claims
api.sig: pub type Claims = {iss: Opt[Str], sub: Opt[Str], aud: List[Str], exp: Opt[Int], nbf: Opt[Int], iat: Opt[Int], jti: Opt[Str]} derive Eq, Show
api.doc:
The registered claims of RFC 7519 section 4.1. `aud` is a list whether the token carries one
string or an array; the times are NumericDates in Unix seconds.

api.name: claims
api.doc: No claims, to fill in with `with`.

api.name: Token
api.sig: pub type Token = {header: JsonValue, claims: Claims, payload: JsonValue, text: Str, alg: Alg, kid: Opt[Str], typ: Opt[Str]} derive Eq, Show
api.doc:
A verified JWT: its JWS header, the registered claims, the whole payload as parsed JSON and
as text (decode it into your own type with `json.decode[T](t.payload)`), and the header's
`alg`, `kid` and `typ`.

api.name: claims_of
api.doc:
The registered claims of a JWT payload, which must be a JSON object, with each registered claim
of the right type.

api.name: claims_json
api.sig: fn claims_json(c: Claims, extra: List[(Str, JsonValue)]) -> Res[JsonValue, JwtErr]
api.doc:
The JSON object of `c`'s claims that are set, then `extra` (your own claims). A name in
`extra` that is also a registered claim set in `c`, or that appears twice, is an error.

api.name: check_claims
api.sig: fn check_claims(t: Token, p: Policy, now: Int) -> Res[Unit, JwtErr]
api.doc:
Checks the claims and the `typ` of a decoded token against `p` at `now` (Unix seconds):
`exp` must be after `now - leeway`, `nbf` at most `now + leeway`, `iat` not after
`now + leeway` (and within `max_age` when set), `iss`, `aud`, `sub` and `typ` as `p` requires,
and every claim in `p.required` present. `typ` compares without case and without an
`application/` prefix (RFC 7515 section 4.1.9).

api.name: verify
api.sig: fn verify(token: Str, keys: List[Key], p: Policy, now: Int) -> Res[Token, JwtErr]
api.doc:
Verifies a JWT: the signature as `jws_verify` does, then the payload as a JSON object with
well-typed registered claims, then `check_claims` at `now` (Unix seconds).

api.name: verify_now
api.sig: fn verify_now(token: Str, keys: List[Key], p: Policy) -> Res[Token, JwtErr] ! time
api.doc: `verify` at the current time.

api.name: decode_jwt_unverified
api.sig: fn decode_jwt_unverified(token: Str, max_len: Int where _ > 0) -> Res[Token, JwtErr]
api.doc: Decodes a JWT without checking its signature or its claims. Never trust what it returns.

api.name: sign
api.sig: fn sign(k: Key, c: Claims, extra: List[(Str, JsonValue)]) -> Res[Str, JwtErr]
api.doc:
Signs a JWT with `k`: header `alg`, `typ: JWT` and `kid` when the key has one; payload the
claims of `c` that are set, then `extra`.

api.name: sign_payload
api.sig: fn sign_payload(k: Key, payload: Str) -> Res[Str, JwtErr]
api.doc:
Signs the JSON object text `payload` as a JWT, for claims written with `json.encode` of your
own record type. The text is signed exactly as given.

api.name: claim
api.sig: fn claim(t: Token, name: Str) -> Opt[JsonValue]
api.doc: The claim `name` of a token's payload, if present.

api.name: claim_str
api.sig: fn claim_str(t: Token, name: Str) -> Opt[Str]
api.doc: The claim `name` if it is a string.

api.name: claim_int
api.sig: fn claim_int(t: Token, name: Str) -> Opt[Int]
api.doc: The claim `name` if it is a number that fits an Int (rounded down).

api.name: claim_bool
api.sig: fn claim_bool(t: Token, name: Str) -> Opt[Bool]
api.doc: The claim `name` if it is a boolean.

api.name: claim_strs
api.sig: fn claim_strs(t: Token, name: Str) -> Opt[List[Str]]
api.doc:
The claim `name` as a list of strings: a string is a list of one, an array must hold only
strings. Scopes and roles are often one of these.

api.name: bearer_token
api.doc: The token of an `Authorization: Bearer <token>` header (RFC 6750), if the request has one.

api.name: parse_jwks
api.doc:
The verifying keys of a public JWK set (RFC 7517 section 5), such as an issuer's
`jwks_uri` document. Ed25519 keys (`kty` OKP, `crv` Ed25519) are read; keys of other types and
curves (RSA, EC, X25519) and keys whose `use` or `key_ops` exclude verification are skipped.
A set that carries private material (`d`, or a symmetric `oct` key) is refused, since
publishing it would have leaked it.

api.name: parse_private_jwks
api.doc:
The keys of a private JWK set: Ed25519 signing keys (with `d`, checked against `x`),
verifying keys, and symmetric `oct` keys, which must name their `alg` so they are bound to it.

api.name: parse_jwk
api.doc: One JWK, private parts allowed; none when it is of a type this package skips.

api.name: public_jwk
api.doc:
The public JWK of `k` (`kty` OKP, `crv` Ed25519, `x`, with `kid`, `alg` and `use` sig), or
none for an HMAC key, which has no public part.

api.name: public_jwks
api.doc: The public JWK set of `keys`, as an issuer publishes it; HMAC keys are left out.

api.name: thumbprint
api.doc:
The RFC 7638 thumbprint of an Ed25519 key (base64url SHA-256 of its canonical JWK, as RFC
8037 section A.3 shows), a common `kid`; none for an HMAC key.
